executive_summary.text: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and the DOJ executed a sweeping takedown of the Lumma Stealer malware-as-a-service platform, seizing or blocking 2,300+ command-and-control domains linked to over 394,000 infected Windows systems globally — though MaaS operators historically rebrand within 30–60 days.

DragonForce ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a coordinated assault on UK retail — hitting M&S (£15M+ estimated daily losses), Co-op (confirmed member data exfiltration), and Harrods in a single week, with M&S initial access attributed to Scattered Spider-style help desk social engineering.

Three chained SonicWall SMA100 vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-32819/32820/32821) allow unauthenticated attackers to achieve root-level remote code execution on VPN appliances widely deployed in SMB and MSP environments — CISA has mandated federal patching by May 22 and Rapid7 published a full exploit chain.

CISA confirmed active nation-state exploitation of two critical Commvault Command Center flaws (CVE-2025-3928, CVSS 9.0 and CVE-2025-34028, CVSS 10.0), targeting backup infrastructure that serves as high-value pre-ransomware staging ground — both carry May 19 KEV deadlines.

Two Scattered Spider (UNC3944) members entered guilty pleas for their roles in the MGM and Caesars attacks, marking a notable DOJ enforcement win against English-language cybercrime groups that rely on SMS phishing, SIM swapping, and identity provider compromise rather than technical exploits.

cyber_news.title: Lumma Stealer MaaS Dismantled — DOJ and Microsoft Seize 2,300+ Domains
cyber_news.summary: A coordinated global law enforcement action involving Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, the DOJ, and international partners dismantled the Lumma Stealer malware-as-a-service infrastructure. Over 2,300 command-and-control domains were seized or blocked, with the operation linked to credential theft impacting 394,000+ Windows systems across financial, healthcare, and education sectors. Criminal charges were filed against the platform's operators.
cyber_news.expanded: Lumma Stealer operated as a polished MaaS offering sold on Russian-language forums, providing affiliates with a web panel for managing stolen credential logs, a builder for customizing payloads, and tiered subscription pricing. The stealer specifically targeted browser-stored credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, session tokens, and 2FA codes — making it particularly effective against targets with cloud-based identity infrastructure. Microsoft's DCU used civil litigation to enable domain seizures under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, complementing DOJ criminal action. The operation's scale — spanning infrastructure across multiple countries — required simultaneous coordination with Europol and INTERPOL. Analysts expect a partial reemergence within 30–60 days under a rebranded identity, consistent with prior MaaS takedowns like Raccoon Stealer.

cyber_news.title: DragonForce Claims UK Retail Trifecta — M&S, Co-op, and Harrods All Hit
cyber_news.summary: DragonForce ransomware group claimed responsibility for attacks against three major UK retailers in a single week: Marks & Spencer (ransomware causing £15M+ estimated daily losses and suspended online orders), Co-op (confirmed data exfiltration of member and employee records), and Harrods (network containment triggered, extent of intrusion under investigation). The M&S intrusion vector was identified as Scattered Spider-style social engineering of the IT help desk to reset credentials and gain initial access.
cyber_news.expanded: The attack pattern across all three retailers closely mirrors the Scattered Spider playbook: initial access via vishing or SMS phishing targeting help desk personnel, followed by identity provider compromise (Okta or equivalent), lateral movement through cloud infrastructure, and eventual ransomware deployment or data exfiltration by a ransomware-as-a-service partner — in this case DragonForce. DragonForce operates a RaaS portal with a 20% revenue share model and has been increasingly linked to Western-nexus initial access brokers. The Co-op incident is particularly significant because the company initially downplayed the breach before DragonForce publicly threatened to release exfiltrated data, forcing a revised disclosure. The concentration of attacks on UK retail within days of each other suggests either a coordinated campaign or opportunistic lateral expansion following success at M&S.

cyber_news.title: SonicWall SMA100 Triple-CVE Chain Enables Unauthenticated Root RCE — CISA KEV
cyber_news.summary: Three chained vulnerabilities in SonicWall SMA100 VPN appliances — CVE-2025-32819, CVE-2025-32820, and CVE-2025-32821 — allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to delete arbitrary files, make filesystem paths writable, and ultimately inject commands executing as root. CISA added all three to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal patch deadline of May 22, 2025. Rapid7 published a full exploit chain proof-of-concept.
cyber_news.expanded: The exploit chain begins with CVE-2025-32819, a path traversal flaw that allows an unauthenticated attacker to delete arbitrary files — including the SonicWall session database, which resets the appliance to a default state with a known admin credential. CVE-2025-32820 is then used to traverse the path and make a target directory world-writable, while CVE-2025-32821 completes the chain by enabling command injection into a diagnostic script executed as root. The combination produces a fully weaponizable, pre-authentication RCE with no user interaction required. SMA100 appliances are frequently deployed as SSL-VPN gateways for SMB and MSP-managed environments, making this vulnerability chain particularly high-impact for the MSP sector. Rapid7's public PoC significantly lowers the bar for less-skilled threat actors.

cyber_news.title: Two Critical Commvault CVEs Actively Exploited by Nation-State Actor — CISA KEV
cyber_news.summary: CISA confirmed active nation-state exploitation of two separate critical flaws in Commvault Command Center: CVE-2025-3928 (CVSS 9.0), an unauthenticated webshell upload vulnerability, and CVE-2025-34028 (CVSS 10.0), a pre-authenticated SSRF-to-RCE via ZIP path traversal. Both carry a May 19 KEV patch deadline. Backup platforms are prime targets for ransomware actors seeking to destroy recovery options prior to encryption.
cyber_news.expanded: CVE-2025-3928 exploits a flaw in Commvault Command Center's Innovation Release that allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload a webshell to a web-accessible directory, achieving persistent remote code execution. CVE-2025-34028, discovered by watchTowr, is a distinct pre-authentication SSRF vulnerability that can be chained with a ZIP path traversal to achieve remote code execution without any credentials — earning a rare CVSS 10.0 score. Nation-state actors targeting backup infrastructure follow a well-established ransomware pre-positioning playbook: compromise backup software first to eliminate recovery options, then deploy ransomware across production systems to maximize leverage. MSPs managing Commvault-based BDR pipelines for clients represent a particularly high-value target, as a single compromised MSP instance could expose multiple downstream client backup environments.

cyber_news.title: Scattered Spider Members Plead Guilty — DOJ Signals Shift in eCrime Prosecution
cyber_news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider group (tracked as UNC3944 and 0ktapus) entered guilty pleas for their roles in the high-profile ransomware attacks against MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment. The prosecutions signal increased DOJ focus and capability in pursuing English-speaking cybercriminal groups that operate through social engineering rather than traditional technical exploits.
cyber_news.expanded: Scattered Spider's operational model is distinct from Eastern European ransomware crews in that it relies heavily on native English fluency to impersonate IT personnel in vishing calls, convincing help desk staff to perform MFA resets, provide temporary VPN credentials, or add attacker-controlled devices to Okta. The group specifically targets identity providers — Okta, Azure AD, and Ping Identity — as the pivot point for lateral movement into cloud environments. In the MGM attack, initial access was reportedly obtained in under 10 minutes via a LinkedIn-researched employee impersonation call to the IT help desk. The guilty pleas are notable because Scattered Spider members are predominantly US and UK nationals in their teens and early twenties, recruited through Telegram and Discord communities known as 'The Com' — a social ecosystem that has proven difficult for law enforcement to infiltrate.

cyber_news.title: Entra ID Cross-Tenant Synchronization Misconfiguration Enables Multi-Tenant Lateral Movement
cyber_news.summary: Security researchers demonstrated that misconfigured Cross-Tenant Synchronization (CTS) policies in Microsoft Entra ID can allow an attacker with limited access in one tenant to propagate identities and permissions to linked partner tenants — a significant supply chain risk for MSPs and MSSPs managing multi-tenant Microsoft 365 environments. Semperis published detailed research on the attack vector.
cyber_news.expanded: Microsoft's CTS feature is designed to synchronize users between business-partner tenants in scenarios like mergers or managed service relationships. However, if an attacker compromises an account with sufficient Entra ID permissions in a source tenant, they can create or modify CTS policies to sync a malicious identity — including role assignments — into target tenants. Because synced accounts often bypass Conditional Access policies that apply to native accounts, the lateral movement can evade standard identity protection controls. In MSP environments where a single Entra ID tenant is used to manage dozens of client tenants via delegated admin or Lighthouse, a single compromised MSP credential can cascade into all downstream client environments. The attack requires no vulnerability in Microsoft's code — it is a logic abuse of a legitimately configured feature.

cyber_news.title: MintsLoader Delivers GhostWeaver RAT via ClickFix Fake CAPTCHA Lures
cyber_news.summary: An active campaign targeting US and European organizations is using ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA pages to deliver the MintsLoader dropper, which subsequently fetches and executes the GhostWeaver remote access trojan. GhostWeaver establishes persistent access via scheduled tasks and communicates with C2 infrastructure over encrypted channels.
cyber_news.expanded: The ClickFix delivery mechanism has become a dominant social engineering lure in 2025: users visiting compromised or malicious websites are presented with a fake CAPTCHA or browser error that instructs them to press Win+R and paste a PowerShell command from their clipboard — which has been silently pre-populated by malicious JavaScript. MintsLoader acts as a lightweight first-stage dropper that performs environment checks (anti-VM, anti-sandbox) before fetching GhostWeaver from a CDN-fronted C2. GhostWeaver is a .NET-based RAT with modular capabilities including keylogging, screenshot capture, credential harvesting from browsers, and lateral movement via WMI. The use of encrypted C2 over HTTPS with domain generation algorithm (DGA) fallback makes GhostWeaver resilient to domain-based blocking. Proofpoint observed this chain being distributed via malicious email attachments linking to the fake CAPTCHA pages.

cyber_news.title: Morphing Meerkat PhaaS Kit Dynamically Spoofs 100+ Brands Using DNS MX Record Lookups
cyber_news.summary: Infoblox researchers identified a phishing-as-a-service platform dubbed 'Morphing Meerkat' that queries the DNS MX record of a target's email domain to determine their mail provider, then dynamically renders a brand-accurate phishing login page — supporting over 100 brand templates. The kit leverages Cloudflare for hosting obfuscation and domain rotation.
cyber_news.expanded: Traditional phishing kits require the attacker to pre-select a target brand. Morphing Meerkat eliminates this friction by automating brand selection: when a victim clicks a phishing link, the kit resolves the domain's MX record, maps the result to a known mail provider (Google, Microsoft, Yahoo, Zoho, etc.), and renders the matching login page in real time. This makes the same phishing infrastructure dynamically accurate for any target email domain, significantly increasing perceived legitimacy. The kit is distributed via spam campaigns using open redirects on adtech infrastructure to bypass URL reputation checks. Exfiltrated credentials are forwarded to attacker-controlled Telegram bots in real time. The DNS-based approach also means that standard phishing detection tools that rely on static brand matching may fail to flag pages served by this kit, as the visual fingerprint changes per visitor.

cyber_news.title: Fake KeePass Site Served via Google Ads Drops Credential-Stealing Malware
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors are running Google Ads campaigns for a convincing KeePass-clone website that delivers credential-stealing malware to users searching for the open-source password manager. The campaign is part of a broader malvertising wave that has previously targeted users searching for 7-Zip, WinSCP, Notepad++, and other developer and security utilities.
cyber_news.expanded: The malvertising chain works by purchasing Google Ads keywords for popular open-source software names, then directing clicks to lookalike domains with near-identical visual design to the legitimate software site. The malware distributed from the KeePass lookalike is a .NET-based stealer that specifically targets browser credential stores, KeePass database files (.kdbx), and crypto wallet seed files — suggesting the operators understand their victim profile well. The ads bypass Google's initial review by staging benign content at the linked URL during the review period, then switching to the malicious payload after approval. Users arrive via a Google-branded ad result, which creates a false sense of legitimacy. Download URLs are typically hosted on cloud storage providers (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3) to further evade URL filtering.

cyber_news.title: NSO Group Pegasus Exploit Chain Revealed in Apple v. NSO Court Filings
cyber_news.summary: Court documents filed in Apple's civil lawsuit against NSO Group detailed the technical workings of BLASTPASS and related zero-click iMessage exploit chains used to deploy Pegasus spyware. Critically, the filings allege NSO operated the targeting infrastructure directly — not just licensing software to customers — with significant legal and export control implications.
cyber_news.expanded: The BLASTPASS exploit chain, first documented by Citizen Lab in 2023, exploited a PassKit (Apple Wallet) processing vulnerability triggered by a malicious attachment sent via iMessage — requiring zero taps or interaction from the victim. Court documents describe NSO's internal tooling, including a web-based dashboard called 'Phantom' used by NSO employees (not just state customers) to initiate targeting operations. This operational involvement distinguishes NSO from a pure software vendor and strengthens Apple's legal theory that NSO is a direct participant in the attacks. The documents also reveal NSO developed at least three distinct iMessage exploit chains over a two-year period (Kismet, ForcedEntry, BLASTPASS), exploiting different memory corruption and logic flaws in image and document parsers, indicating sustained internal R&D capacity against Apple's closed ecosystem.

cyber_news.title: NIST Publishes CSF 2.0 Quick-Start Implementation Guides Tailored for Small Businesses
cyber_news.summary: NIST released updated implementation guidance for the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 specifically targeting small and medium-sized businesses, including sector-specific templates and practical materials for the new 'Govern' function. The guides provide MSPs with client-facing resources for building and presenting compliance programs aligned to the current framework version.
cyber_news.expanded: CSF 2.0 introduced the 'Govern' function as a sixth core pillar alongside Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover — reflecting a maturation in thinking about cybersecurity as an organizational governance discipline rather than purely a technical one. The new SMB quick-start guides include pre-built Community Profiles for sectors including healthcare, manufacturing, and financial services, as well as a baseline 'small business' profile designed for organizations without dedicated security staff. For MSPs, these profiles provide a defensible framework structure for vCISO engagements, client risk assessments, and compliance gap analyses — particularly as cyber insurance underwriters increasingly reference CSF alignment in their questionnaires.

deep_dive.title: Lumma Stealer Global Takedown — Infrastructure, Scope, and What Comes Next
deep_dive.content: The Lumma Stealer disruption represents one of the most operationally significant MaaS takedowns of 2025. Lumma (also known as LummaC2) operated as a full-featured infostealer-as-a-service platform sold on Russian-language cybercrime forums at subscription tiers ranging from $250 to $1,000/month. The platform provided affiliates with a polished web panel for sorting stolen credential logs by geography and data type, a payload builder with anti-analysis options, and a network of resilient C2 domains using domain generation algorithms for fallback. The stealer specifically targeted browser-saved credentials, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallet files, and TOTP seeds — enabling account takeover even against MFA-protected accounts via session token theft. Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit executed the takedown using civil litigation under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, naming LummaC2's operator ('Shamel') and enabling domain seizures across registrars in multiple jurisdictions. Simultaneously, the DOJ filed criminal charges and coordinated with Europol and INTERPOL to disrupt backend infrastructure. Sectors most heavily impacted included financial services, healthcare, and higher education. Despite the scale of the action, analysts widely expect a reemergence under a rebranded identity within 30–60 days — as seen with Raccoon Stealer v2 following its 2022 disruption — making proactive IOC feed updates and EDR rule refreshes essential for defenders.

biggest_hacks.title: M&S Ransomware Attack — DragonForce Claims Responsibility, £15M+ Daily Losses Ongoing
biggest_hacks.summary: Marks & Spencer suffered a crippling ransomware attack attributed to DragonForce — with initial access achieved via Scattered Spider-style IT help desk social engineering — suspending online orders, disrupting contactless payments, and generating estimated losses exceeding £15M per day.

biggest_hacks.title: Co-op Cyberattack — DragonForce Confirms Exfiltration of Millions of Member Records
biggest_hacks.summary: Co-op initially downplayed its cyberattack before DragonForce publicly threatened to release exfiltrated data, forcing the retailer to confirm that customer and employee data — including Co-op member records — had been accessed and stolen.

biggest_hacks.title: TeleMessage Signal Clone Used by U.S. Officials Breached — Archived Government Messages Exposed
biggest_hacks.summary: TeleMessage, a third-party Signal-archiving application used by NSC staff and other U.S. government officials, was breached by an attacker who accessed archived messages, contact directories, and backend infrastructure data — prompting the app's suspension.

biggest_hacks.title: SK Telecom SIM Data Breach — 27 Million Subscribers' USIM Data Compromised
biggest_hacks.summary: South Korea's largest telecommunications carrier confirmed that USIM data for approximately 27 million subscribers was exfiltrated after malware was deployed on Home Subscriber Server infrastructure, prompting a government-mandated SIM card replacement program.

biggest_hacks.title: Nova Scotia Power / Emera Ransomware Attack — Canadian Utility IT Systems Compromised
biggest_hacks.summary: Nova Scotia Power and its parent company Emera confirmed a ransomware attack affected corporate IT systems, with the utility stating operational technology was isolated but acknowledging potential customer data exposure.

biggest_hacks.title: Harrods Cyberattack — Third Major UK Retailer Targeted in One Week
biggest_hacks.summary: Harrods confirmed it was targeted in a cyberattack and restricted internet access to its systems as a containment measure — becoming the third major UK retailer hit within a single week alongside M&S and Co-op, with DragonForce or affiliated actors suspected.

vulnerabilities.description: Three-CVE chain enabling unauthenticated remote root code execution: CVE-2025-32819 deletes arbitrary files (including session DB to reset admin credentials), CVE-2025-32820 makes directories world-writable via path traversal, and CVE-2025-32821 injects commands executing as root. Rapid7 published a full PoC. CISA KEV deadline May 22. Update to firmware 10.2.1.14-82sv or later.

Pre-authentication SSRF vulnerability chained with ZIP path traversal enables remote code execution with no credentials required. Discovered by watchTowr. Nation-state actors are actively targeting backup infrastructure as a ransomware pre-positioning tactic. CISA KEV deadline May 19.

Unauthenticated webshell upload vulnerability in Commvault Command Center allowing persistent remote code execution. Actively exploited by a confirmed nation-state threat actor per CISA advisory. MSPs managing client BDR pipelines on Commvault are at elevated supply-chain risk. CISA KEV deadline May 19.

Insufficient policy enforcement in Chrome's Loader component allows cross-origin data theft via a crafted HTML page. Actively exploited in the wild prior to patch availability. Update all managed Chrome instances to 136.0.7103.113 or later. CISA KEV deadline May 26.

vulnerabilities.product: Microsoft Windows (DWM Core Library / CLFS Driver)
vulnerabilities.description: Three Windows local privilege escalation vulnerabilities — two in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver and one in DWM Core Library — exploited in targeted attacks. CLFS is a recurring post-exploitation escalation path used by ransomware actors to achieve SYSTEM privileges after initial access. Patched in May 2025 Patch Tuesday. CISA KEV deadline May 27.

Pre-authentication directory traversal in Output Messenger server allows arbitrary file read and write operations, exploited by Turkish state-nexus APT Marbled Dust to deploy persistent backdoors against Kurdish-linked targets. Limited deployment scope reduces overall exposure but nation-state attribution elevates priority for any affected deployments. CISA KEV deadline May 22.
